display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Web frontend pack. Every question has a recommended answer,
so Accept all works
A reference site: none, use a clean neutral
Brand: slate, with one indigo accent. Density: balanced
Theme: both, following the system. Font: the system stack
Kit: shadcn/ui on Tailwind, source copied into the repo
An existing repo extracts Tailwind, CSS variables and the
component folder, and shows them for confirmation instead of asking

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Phase 0, before any screen worker
tokens.json, W3C design tokens. Color roles, six type steps,
4 px spacing, radii, shadows, motion. Light and dark
CSS variables and the Tailwind theme are generated, not hand-edited

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One kit. Button, Card, Input, Table, Dialog, Toast, page header
Each has variants and the states default, hover, focus,
disabled, loading and error
Templates: app shell, page header with an actions slot,
list/detail, form, empty, error

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
/__styleguide renders every primitive, variant, state
and template, in light and dark
Screenshots at desktop, tablet and phone are the reference crops
when the developer supplied none
Conventions are quoted into briefs: page header for titles,
primary actions in the header slot, Table rather than a custom grid

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A screen task gets a spec, not a picture
Route, template, regions, states, density, and which crops to match
The accessible names are also the test contract
A box-and-label wireframe can be approved in the plan preview
Workers compose the kit. They do not invent look-alikes
They may only use tokens

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
After the task
Block: raw colors, arbitrary pixels, new fonts, look-alike components
Block serious axe-core issues: labels, roles, contrast, focus
Block layout at three widths: no overflow, overlap or clipping,
tap targets at least 24 px
Warn: header height, page padding and spacing rhythm
Advise only: a Senior vision review against the crops
Pixel diff blocks only after the developer approves a baseline

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
App tab runs harness/integration, or a chosen feature branch,
in its own browser port and profile

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Point mode. Hover outlines. A click captures
route, role, accessible name, DOM path,
component and source file and line from the dev-only plugin,
a highlighted crop, computed spacing and type,
and the owning task from path ownership
The composer target becomes that element
A dragged box can point at a gap between elements

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: What was asked?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A visual change for that feature's owner
Example: KitchenCard padding down one spacing step

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A change to the screen spec
Example: Print moves into the page-header actions slot
Tests find it by role and name, so the journey still passes

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Who owns the file?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: That feature's owner. A normal change

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
The design-system owner
Preview the affected screens before applying

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The owning feature, as an override inside tokens

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: The project planner. Brownfield code outside the plan

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
When it finishes: before and after, side by side
Accepting updates the approved baseline
Anything still off is another message

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
A screenshot mid-build becomes a crop for the screens it covers
The design owner checks tokens and previews the effect first
Two workers want the same new primitive: one is built, both use it
'Make this red' uses a token role or a named variant. Raw values stay blocked
If the preview will not start: show the error and the owning task,
and offer the last good build
No design system yet: extract what exists, offer to consolidate tokens,
never restyle the whole app unasked
